1.why: Every screen is a static, sparse layout of plain cards with no animations, moving images, or pop-up dialogs anywhere in the flow.

2.why: Primary buttons are bold dark-blue, the current step chip is highlighted, and feedback is green, but the critical security codes sit in a plain monospace 'Logs' panel at the page bottom rather than standing out near the input fields.

3.why: Each page presents one task with a clear label and a 'Next:' banner, but finding the code to enter requires scrolling past the form to the Logs section.

4.why: A 5-step progress indicator, per-step 'Next:' banners, on-screen codes in Logs, and inline password rules reduce memorization, though the user must still transcribe a long token from the Logs panel into the field.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, no password-manager or autofill affordance, and no saved-credential option appears on any screen, only bare input fields.

6.why: The Logs panel persistently accumulates previously delivered items (recovery token, security codes, completion entries) across screens, so prior items remain visible and recognizable.

7.why: All copy is short plain sentences, e.g. 'Use 12 or more characters with uppercase, lowercase, a number, and a symbol' and 'Select send, then use the practice code in Logs.'

8.why: No error state or error message appears in any of the 14 screenshots, so the descriptiveness of error handling cannot be confirmed or denied.

9.why: Steps give instructions ('Select send, then use the practice code in Logs') and the Logs show actual codes, but no format examples are provided, e.g. no sample email or example password.

10.why: No choice among authentication methods exists—there is only password plus security code, no face-login or alternative—while the few choices that do exist (accept vs. sign out, use token or enter manually) are labeled clearly.

11.why: Every screen offers essentially one primary action ('Request recovery code', 'Confirm security code', 'Change password safely', 'Accept updated privacy conditions'), so the user never faces more than one or two options at once.

12.why: Each action produces an explicit outcome message: 'A security code has been prepared for this practice session', 'Password confirmed. Next, confirm your security code', 'Password changed', and 'Privacy conditions accepted. Hospital authorities can now help book the appointment.'

13.why: A 'Help and safe sign-in reminders' panel and a changing 'Next:' tip banner appear on every step, though the help text is identical on all screens and includes developer-oriented wording like 'https://localhost' and 'practice Logs'.

14.why: A 'Forgot your password? Start recovery' link offers a restart path and no lockouts are shown, but no mistake or retry scenario is demonstrated in the screenshots.

15.why: All 14 screens share the identical header, navigation links, step chips, card layout, button styling, help panel, and Logs section, making the design highly consistent throughout the flow.
